Change Request: Tiered tests: make the checks before a pull request faster without weakening the gate. (1) Measure first: run the full suite with --durations and record where the time goes. (2) A quick local tier (compile + the tests of the changed area + a small core: api smoke, fresh database, security, release gate / integrity) for building and before opening a PR; (3) mark the slow tests (migrations from older releases, staging / restore, records archive) so a quick run can skip them; (4) run the suite in parallel (pytest-xdist, dev-only) if the measurement shows the tests are independent; (5) cache the older-release databases the migrations test builds (they never change for a given commit). The full suite stays the required check in CI on every pull request, and is run locally only when a change touches migrations, release controls or security.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-23: the full local suite takes 13 to 16 minutes per change (about 710 tests in 56 files; 43 files boot their own server, the migrations test builds and upgrades a database from each of 55 older releases every run). CI takes about 5 to 6 minutes on Linux. The last CI-only failures (KW-62, KW-66, KW-68) were Linux versus Windows differences that a full local run does not catch, so CI is the real gate. Not measured yet: the speed-ups are proposals until a --durations run shows the slowest tests.
Acceptance Criteria: A timings report (--durations) is recorded; a documented quick tier that runs in about 3 minutes or less locally; slow tests marked and skippable; the full suite still runs unchanged in CI as the required check and before any release; if parallel runs are adopted, the suite passes repeatedly in parallel and in CI with no flaky failures; legacy-commit upgrade checks still run in CI; CLAUDE.md and docs/release-guide.md describe the tiers and when to use each.

(2) Show a clear warning to administrators and Quality Managers when 'Verify audit trail' fails or has not been run for a set time (today a broken chain blocks nothing). Release, CoA and recall records are what auditors and customers rely on. A change to an audit control needs a Quality Manager note (QM-001) and an update of the data-integrity statement.

Change Request: Declare foreign keys for the *_id columns that have none, so the database itself refuses a row that points at something that does not exist. SQLite cannot add a foreign key to an existing table, so each affected table must be rebuilt (create new, copy, check, swap) inside the existing one-transaction migration with a pre-migration snapshot. Start with an inventory of the columns and the tables that hold real data, then rebuild in small steps with a check that no row is orphaned before the foreign key is added.
Context / Rationale: Hardening review of 2026-10-24, finding R-31 (partly fixed in batch 7: status triggers and non-negative quantities exist; many *_id columns still have no foreign key). Section: Lots: who may edit lot information, and its change history
Change Request: Only administrators can change lot information after a lot has been added to KelpWorks, and every change is fully traceable. Today (1) a lot's supplier, supplier lot number, expiry date, PO / reference, notes and hold status can be changed by a Quality Manager or an administrator, (2) a use can be moved from one lot to another by either, and (3) a delivery's details (supplier, invoice number and date, PO, order number, delivery document, carrier, ship date, currency, freight, tax, invoice total, condition on arrival, notes) can be corrected by ANY signed-in user. Make all of these administrator-only, enforced by the server (403 for everyone else) and with the buttons hidden for other users. Receiving a lot stays open to everyone who can receive today. Traceability: every change records who, when, which field, the old value, the new value and the reason (a reason is required), in append-only history that no one can edit or delete (extend what exists: consumable_lot_log and receipt_log). Show ONE history per lot that combines the lot's own changes with its delivery's changes (and moved uses), newest first, and make it exportable (CSV) for an audit or a recall. Record a refused attempt by a non-administrator (who, when, what they tried) so it is visible. Documents already attached to a delivery stay add-only (never deleted). Quantities keep their existing rules (stock changes only through the ledger: receive, use, Adjust, Count).
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26. A lot record is the link in recall traceability (supplier lot -> runs -> finished goods -> customers, KW-71 / the recall report), so changing its supplier lot number, expiry or supplier after receipt can silently break a trace; only a small, accountable group should be able to do it, with a visible reason and history. Current code: PUT /api/lots/<id> and POST /api/lots/uses/<id>/move allow administrator OR Quality Manager (route_lots, can_edit); PUT /api/receipts/<id> (the delivery window) has no role check, only a reason when a filled-in value changes; both write append-only logs (consumable_lot_log, receipt_log) but there is no single combined history per lot. Related: KW-23 / KW-81 (approved suppliers), KW-82 (receive from a document, delivery fields), KW-86 (item identity edits need a reason once received), KW-54 (receiving workflow validation, run after this), KW-60 (lots are re-received after the wipe). Must NOT change: how lots are received, stock quantities, existing lots and their history, the lot trace and recall report. QM-001: lot control and traceability records are touched, so a change note for the Quality Manager is needed. OPEN DECISION raised with this item: should a Quality Manager who is not an administrator still be able to PLACE a lot on hold / release a hold? Recommendation: yes for hold only (a safety action, still logged with a reason); everything else administrator-only.

Section: Safety data sheets: a recorded review date; the supplier Documents count
Change Request: Two parts. PART 1 - record a review of a safety data sheet (SDS) separately from the manufacturer's issue date. The issue date comes from the file name in SharePoint and the manufacturer controls it, so it cannot be used to show that KelpWorks reviewed the sheet. Add a 'Last reviewed on' date per SDS that an administrator OR a Quality Manager can record (server-enforced: anyone else gets 403; the button is shown only to them), with an optional note. The date cannot be in the future and a review cannot be recorded before the issue date. Review due = (the later of the issue date and the last reviewed date) + the review interval (setting sds_review_years, unchanged, same for every sheet); review soon / overdue work as today. The issue date is never changed and keeps showing as the manufacturer printed it. Each review is an append-only entry in the sheet's History (who, when, reviewed-on date, old -> new review due, note); a new revision of the sheet with a later issue date restarts the clock as today and the earlier reviews stay in the history. Show 'Last reviewed' (date and who) in the Documents > Safety data sheets table and in the supplier panel's SDS list. A per-sheet interval is NOT part of this item. PART 2 - the Documents number in the Suppliers list must include linked SDS. Today it counts only the documents uploaded on the supplier, so linking an SDS does not change it. Make it supplier documents + the current linked SDS (a withdrawn sheet is not counted), and show the split so it stays clear (for example '3 (1 SDS)'). The expired / expiring / SDS-overdue badges keep working.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26. The SDS review due date is the issue date + 3 years for every sheet (sds_review in kelp_erp_server.py, setting sds_review_years), and the only way to restart it today is a new file with a later date in the SharePoint folder; renaming a file to a review date would misstate the manufacturer's issue date, which an auditor could question. A separate, logged 'last reviewed' date is the honest record that the company checked the sheet and found it current. Part 2: the Suppliers list column Documents is 'nDocs' = len(supplier documents) (KW-81); since KW-83 SDS are loaded in Documents and linked to the supplier, so they appear in the supplier panel but not in the count. Related: KW-83 (SDS linked to suppliers), KW-81 (Suppliers page), KW-23. Rule 5 in CLAUDE.md applies: the Calculations page entry for the safety data sheet review date must be updated to the new formula. Must NOT change: the issue date read from the file name, the SharePoint-as-master rule, how sheets are accepted / revised / withdrawn, supplier document handling. QM-001: document control (review of controlled documents) is touched, so a change note for the Quality Manager is needed; docs/data-integrity-statement.md and docs/controlled-documents.md need the new control. Open question for later: whether the Quality Manager's review should also need a password re-entry like a signature (not assumed here).
Acceptance Criteria: An administrator or Quality Manager can record 'Last reviewed on' (not in the future, not before the issue date, optional note) for a safety data sheet; a Production Manager or plain user gets 403 and does not see the button; Review due = later of issue date and last reviewed + the interval, with ok / soon / overdue as today; the issue date is unchanged; each review is logged in the sheet's History (who, when, date, old -> new review due, note) and cannot be edited or deleted; a new revision with a later issue date restarts the clock and keeps the earlier reviews in the history; 'Last reviewed' (date and who) shows in the Documents SDS table and the supplier panel; the Calculations page entry for the SDS review date shows the new formula; the Suppliers list Documents number = supplier documents + current linked SDS (withdrawn excluded) and shows the split; the supplier flags (documents expired / expiring, SDS overdue) behave as before; tests cover both roles and the refusals, the date rules, the review-due formula, the history, the new-revision case and the count; the Quality Manager is told (QM-001 note) and the docs name the control.
Notes: PR #109 merged 2026-10-26 (merge 464d039; CI test green; full suite 876 passed) and live on Render. PART 1: an administrator or a Quality Manager can record a review of a safety data sheet (Documents > Safety data sheets > Record review...): date not in the future and not before the issue date, optional note; a Production Manager or plain user is refused (403); a withdrawn sheet cannot be reviewed. Last reviewed shows in the Documents table and the supplier panel; the Calculations entry shows the new formula. PART 2: the Suppliers list Documents number = supplier documents + current linked SDS, shown as 3 (1 SDS); withdrawn sheets not counted. Section: Item names: system keys, a locked Used IBC pool, rename, a default reagent by item number (phase 1)
Touches: Production log; Pre-processing; Inventory items; Database / schema
Change Request: PHASE 1 (this item). Make an inventory item's identity the item number / id and its name only a label, so a standard item can be renamed safely, and lock the one item that must never change. (1) SYSTEM KEYS: give the standard items the code finds BY NAME today a stable internal key (Citric Acid, Potassium Sorbate, Sodium Benzoate, New 1,000 L IBC Tote, Used 1,000 L IBC Tote, and any other standard item created at start-up). Assign the keys once at upgrade from their current names (run_once) and, for a new database, after the seed. Every place that finds them by name uses the key instead: the Used IBC pool in production finalize and pre-processing completion and the data integrity check, the creation of the standard items at every start (so a renamed item is never recreated beside itself), the clean-start tool's SYSTEM_ITEMS, the reagent default and the legacy fallbacks. No behaviour change for today's data. (2) LOCK 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote': it cannot be renamed, disposed or deleted, have its unit or container flag changed, or be replaced, even by an administrator (the server refuses; the buttons are hidden and the item shows a lock); only a code change can alter it. (3) RENAME an item, reagents and CIP agents first (including Citric Acid RGT-001 and Potassium Sorbate): ADMINISTRATOR ONLY (403 for anyone else, the Edit window shows the Name field only to administrators), a reason is required, the change is logged append-only (who, when, old name, new name, reason). Names stay unique, also against names kept as aliases. The item number, id, lots, ledger and links never change; the old name is kept as an alias (it cannot be given to a different item, and a lookup by the old name still resolves). Signed run records, lot numbers and past receipts keep the name text they were written with (no rewriting of history). (4) DEFAULT ITEM PER REAGENT TYPE BY ITEM NUMBER: an administrator chooses which item is the default for Citric Acid / Potassium Sorbate / Sodium Benzoate (by item number, logged), replacing 'the item named exactly like the type comes first'; the production-log pickers preselect it (an organic product still offers organic items first, as today). On upgrade the default is the item that is first today, so nothing changes until an administrator changes it. PHASE 2 (a separate item, after phase 1 is live): rename of containers, labels and 'New 1,000 L IBC Tote' (needs the dependent finished-good label items and the name-text references of run packaging, pre-processing packs and sample points updated or aliased in the same step).
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26, who will add real reagents (citric acid, potassium sorbate) and packaging (new 1,000 L IBC totes) after the KW-60 clean start and wants the standard items to carry their real names. Findings in the code: runs find reagents by Reagent type and item id (not by name), but the reagent default is 'the item named exactly like the type' (_reagent_items orders by name = type), 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' is found by exact name in production finalize, pre-processing completion and the integrity check, the start-up steps create / rename the standard items by name (so renaming 'New 1,000 L IBC Tote' would likely create a second one at the next start), and the clean-start tool keeps four items by exact name (SYSTEM_ITEMS). Containers are also referenced by NAME TEXT in run packaging rows, pre-processing packs, finished-goods lot numbers, sample points and the finished-good label items, which is why container rename is phase 2. Best practice agreed: identity = item number / id, bind code to stable keys not names, rename admin-only with a reason and a log, keep an alias, do not rewrite signed history, explicit default per type by item number. DECISIONS made 2026-10-26: (1) 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' is locked even against administrators (only a code change can alter it); (2) rename is administrator only. Related: KW-86 (item identity, an item's name never changes there until this item), KW-60 (clean start), KW-23 / KW-81. Must NOT change: existing item names and numbers at upgrade, lots, receipts, the ledger and signed run records, how stock moves. QM-001: item master data and change control are touched, so a note for the Quality Manager is needed; docs/data-integrity-statement.md and CLAUDE.md need updating (the 'an item's name never changes' statements).
Acceptance Criteria: After upgrade every standard item has its key and every lookup that used a name uses the key, with no change in behaviour on today's data (runs, pre-processing, integrity check, start-up creation, clean-start tool and its test, legacy-upgrade check); a renamed standard item is not recreated at the next start; 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' cannot be renamed, disposed, deleted, changed (unit / container flag) or replaced by anyone including an administrator, the server refuses and the UI shows a lock; an administrator can rename a reagent or CIP item (including Citric Acid and Potassium Sorbate) with a required reason, anyone else gets 403 and no Name field; the rename is logged append-only (who, when, old, new, reason), names stay unique including aliases, the old name is kept as an alias that resolves and cannot be reused for another item; item number, id, lots, ledger, receipts and signed run records are unchanged; an administrator can set the default item per reagent type by item number (logged) and the production-log pickers preselect it, an organic product still offers organic items first, and on upgrade the default equals today's first item; tests cover the keys, the locks, the rename permissions and log, the alias, the default setting and picker, the restart-does-not-recreate case and the clean-start tool; the Quality Manager is told (QM-001 note) and the docs are updated; phase 2 is raised as its own item after phase 1 is live.
Notes: PR #111 merged 2026-10-26 (merge a06f4a3; CI test green; full suite 890 passed, 1 skipped, plus one Windows connection abort in test_staging that passed on rerun) and live on Render. PHASE 1: the standard items (Citric Acid, Potassium Sorbate, Sodium Benzoate, the CIP agents, the IBC totes, the drum, the sample vessels) carry a stable key and the code finds them by key; a renamed Sodium Benzoate or CIP agent is no longer created a second time at start-up. 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' is locked (no rename or change by anyone, including an administrator; stock can still be counted, received and written off). An administrator can rename a reagent or CIP item with a required reason: logged, the old name kept as an alias and never reusable, item number / lots / records unchanged; containers and labels are refused until phase 2. An administrator sets the default item per reagent type by item number (logged); the production-log picker preselects it. The clean-start tool finds its four system items by key. QM-001: a row for this is to be added to the combined note (QM-001_Rev5.1_change_note_KW-82_KW-86_KW-88_DRAFT.md). PHASE 2 (container, label and New 1,000 L IBC Tote rename, with the dependent label items and name-text references) is to be raised as its own item.

Section: Item names, phase 2: rename containers, labels and New 1,000 L IBC Tote
Touches: Production log; Pre-processing; Inventory items; Samples; Finished goods / shipping; Database / schema
Change Request: PHASE 2 of KW-89 (phase 1 is live). Let an administrator rename containers (packaging output units and sample-point vessels), the finished-good label items and the 'New 1,000 L IBC Tote' item, with the same rules as phase 1: administrator only (403 for anyone else), a required reason, an append-only log (who, when, old name, new name, reason), names unique including old names, the old name kept as an alias, item number / id / lots / ledger unchanged. 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' stays locked. A container's name is also stored as TEXT in many records, so the rename must handle every one of them (see Context): (1) the start-up creation of the drum, the sample vessels and the label items (for 'New 1,000 L IBC Tote' and '55 gallon drum') uses the item keys, so a renamed one is never created again; (2) the Sample Point defaults that name '50 mL falcon tube' and '100 g sample bag' use the keys; (3) a package counts as an IBC from an explicit flag on the item, not because its name contains 'IBC', so a renamed tote still counts as an IBC in a run's output; (4) the finished-good label items follow their container: renaming a container renames its label items ('FG Label - <product> - <container>') and updates their package link in the same step, each change logged, and a label item cannot be renamed on its own; (5) lookups by container name text (the Packaging table, pre-processing pack-out, sample points, amending a finalized run, stock commits, the CSV stock update) resolve an old name through the alias to the renamed item; (6) text already stored in finished production logs, finished-goods lot numbers (they are printed on the IBCs), shipments and signed snapshots is NOT rewritten (the record keeps what it said); new entries use the new name. The pickers show the current name.
Context / Rationale: Raised 2026-10-26 as the follow-up to KW-89 phase 1 (PR 111) at N. Wrana's request, so the real names can be given to the standard packaging items (for example a manufacturer-specific 1,000 L IBC tote) once reagents are renamed. Why this is not in phase 1: a container's name is used as text, not only as an id, in run_packaging_entries.container_unit, run_sample_points.container, preproc_packaging.container, fg_lots.package_size and finished-goods lot numbers (<processing lot>-<container name>), in the finished-good label items (label_package and the name 'FG Label - <product> - <container>'), in the Packaging picker (packaging_container_litres_map) and in the IBC count (a package is an IBC when its name contains 'IBC'); the start-up steps create the drum, the sample vessels and the labels by name; the Sample Point defaults name two vessels. The one-time helper _rename_consumable already propagates a rename into run_packaging_entries, run_sample_points and fg_lots, which shows the references that exist. Packaging rows are part of the signed production-log snapshot, so rewriting them would change the hash (RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_VERSION / rebaseline): the recommended approach keeps stored text as written and resolves old names through the alias. OPEN DECISION raised with this item: alias lookups with stored text unchanged (recommended) versus moving the references to item ids and rebaselining signed records. Related: KW-89 (phase 1), KW-86, KW-60 (clean start). Must NOT change: existing records, lot numbers, signed run snapshots, stock quantities. QM-001: item master data again; extend the combined change note (the container rename row and decisions D12 / D13).
Acceptance Criteria: An administrator can rename a container, a label's container and 'New 1,000 L IBC Tote' with a required reason; anyone else gets 403; the rename is logged append-only and the old name is kept as an alias that cannot be reused; 'Used 1,000 L IBC Tote' stays locked; a renamed container is not created again at the next start (drum, sample vessels, label items) and still works in the Packaging picker, Sample Point defaults, pre-processing pack-out and amend of a finalized run; a renamed tote still counts as an IBC in a run's output; renaming a container renames its label items and updates their package link, each change logged, and a label item cannot be renamed alone; names already stored in finished production logs, finished-goods lot numbers, shipments and signed snapshots are unchanged and still verify (release hash unchanged); lookups by the old name still resolve; item number, id, lots and ledger unchanged; tests cover each rule above, the restart-does-not-recreate case, the IBC flag, the label follow-up, the alias lookups, the signed-log hash and the clean-start tool; the Quality Manager is told (QM-001 note) and the docs are updated.
Notes: Released 2026-10-26 (PR 113, d9e0bc1). Containers, labels and the New 1,000 L IBC Tote can be renamed by an administrator; records keep the written name (decision A); IBC counted from a flag. QM-001 note rows S15, D14, D15 (not yet entered in the manual).

Section: Lots: correct cost, pack and quantity after receiving
Change Request: After a lot has been received, an administrator can correct three things on that lot: (1) unit cost (the price per stock unit, and the line total when there is one); (2) pack type (the "received as" text, for example "45 x Box, 50 lb", and the pack link used to convert it); (3) quantity received. Administrator only: a Quality Manager cannot. A reason is required for each change. Every change is logged to the lot's append-only history (who, when, old -> new, reason), like the existing lot corrections (Inventory Items > the item's Lots > Trace > Correct details). A quantity change moves stock through the normal stock path as one ledger line ("Receipt correction", the lot as its reference): the item's on-hand and the lot's remaining quantity change by the difference. A quantity change cannot take the lot's remaining quantity below what has already been used; the message tells the administrator to resolve the uses first.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26. Today an administrator or Quality Manager can correct a lot's supplier, supplier lot, expiry, PO and notes (KW-87 was withdrawn because that already works), but unit cost, pack type and quantity cannot be changed at all. A wrong price, pack or count at receiving can only be fixed by a stock adjustment, which leaves the lot itself wrong. Follow the Correct details pattern. Assumptions for Claude Code to confirm in its plan: (1) a lot correction does not change the item's own cost per unit; (2) production runs and the signed release records are not touched (they store the item, not the lot cost); (3) the correction is also noted on the lot's delivery log when the lot belongs to a delivery; (4) an expired or held lot can still be corrected; (5) not part of the signed snapshot. Stock only moves through _consume. QM-001 impact: receiving and lot control, so a Quality Manager note is needed.
Acceptance Criteria: Only an administrator can change a received lot's unit cost, pack type or quantity (403 for a Quality Manager and everyone else). A reason is required (400 without). Each change appears in the lot's history with old -> new, who and when, and unit cost and pack type are shown in the lot trace. A quantity change writes one ledger line and moves the item's on-hand and the lot's remaining quantity by the difference; a change that would take the remaining quantity below what was used is refused with a clear message. The lot's delivery shows the correction. Tests cover each rule; the full suite passes; the screen is checked in the browser; the Quality Manager is told (QM-001 note).
Notes: Released 2026-10-26 (PR 115, f016365). A Quality Manager or administrator can correct a received lot's unit cost, line amount, pack and quantity (POST /api/lots/<id>/correct, reason required, logged on the lot and its delivery; stock moves by the difference as one ledger line; cannot go below what was used). Decision N. Wrana: Quality Manager allowed too. QM-001 note rows S16, D16, D17 (not yet entered in the manual). Follow-ups: KW-92 (add a new pack in the window), KW-93.

Section: Lots: add a new pack when correcting a received lot
Change Request: In a received lot's "Correct receipt…" window, the Pack field offers the item's existing packs and "+ New pack…" (name and quantity per stock unit). The new pack is saved on the item (and logged in the pack log, as a pack added at receiving is today) and used for that lot. The number of packs sets the quantity received exactly as in KW-91. The same Quality Manager or administrator rule as KW-91 applies. Also check that the existing Correct details window lets the same people fix a wrong pack where it is shown, so a received lot's pack type can be changed either by selecting an existing pack or by adding a new one.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26: "I'm still not able to update the pack type (add new one and/or select from existing) received lot". Follows KW-91 (PR 115, merged or not at the time of building: check), which lets an administrator or Quality Manager select one of the item's EXISTING packs but gives no way to create one; if KW-91 is not yet live on the site the request was tested on, the user will not see even the selection. A pack is stored only as text on the lot (received_as) plus the item's consumable_packs list. Reuse the existing pack creation rules (anyone may add a pack; a duplicate name is not added twice; every add goes to the append-only pack log). The item's stock unit never changes. No schema change expected.
Acceptance Criteria: In Correct receipt, a user who may correct a lot can choose an existing pack or create a new one (name, quantity per stock unit) without leaving the window; the new pack appears on the item and in the pack log, and the lot shows "N x <pack>" with the quantity received = packs x quantity per pack (a ledger line if the quantity changes, as in KW-91). A duplicate pack name is not added twice; a bad quantity per pack is refused. A user who may not correct a lot cannot. Tests cover each rule; the screen is checked in the browser; the full suite passes.

Section: Receive: attach an invoice once per delivery
Change Request: When several items are received from the same invoice (one delivery: same supplier and invoice number), uploading the same file again for the next item must not add another copy. If an identical file (same content) is already attached to that delivery, Receive skips it and tells the person "already attached". A different file, even with the same name, is still added. The nightly records archive therefore gets the document once.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-26: when several reagents are line items on the same invoice, uploading the invoice once per reagent makes it show up repeated for each lot. Cause found: Receive handles one item at a time and correctly reuses the delivery (same supplier + invoice number, _receipt_for), but _store_receipt_attachment stores every uploaded file as a new receipt_attachments row with no check for an identical file, so the delivery lists the same invoice once per reagent and the storage quota is charged each time. Assumptions for Claude Code to confirm in its plan: (1) existing duplicate copies stay as they are (a document is never deleted); only new duplicates are prevented; (2) "identical" means the same file content (compare a hash of the bytes; a stored hash column would be an additive change, or compare the stored files of that delivery); (3) the KW-82 reading flow, which attaches the uploaded document as an invoice on Receive, follows the same rule; (4) the skipped upload is not charged to the storage room or the daily upload quota. QM-001 impact: none expected (the document is still on the delivery); say so at release.
Acceptance Criteria: Receiving three different reagents from one invoice and uploading the same invoice file each time leaves exactly one copy on the delivery; the second and third receives say it was already attached and succeed. A different file (or the same name with different content) is still attached. The skipped upload does not count toward the storage room or the daily upload quota. The records archive lists the document once. The Receive window, the delivery window and the lot trace each show it once. Existing duplicates are not removed or changed. Tests cover each rule; the screen is checked in the browser; the full suite passes.

Section: Release status, checklist and hold reasons
Change Request: Make the state of the release workflow and the reason for a hold visible and tidy. (1) Release status line: on each run in Product Release (the list and the run window) show one status line naming the stage (Pending review, Awaiting Quality release, Released, On hold, Rejected), who it is waiting on, and the next step. Example: 'On hold. Cause: lab result for Salmonella voided by N. Wrana on 27 Oct. Needs: a new passing result, then a Quality Manager releases from hold.' (2) Release checklist: a tidy checklist of green / red items in the style of the production log's required-fields chips: production log reviewed; each release gate test met (the existing release_gate result, with its reason); lab report attached where the gate requires it; every out-of-specification result has a release comment; production log unchanged since review (hash matches); no open amendment. Each red item says what to do and opens the right window (for example 'Add lab result'). (3) Hold reason next to every Hold badge: on the Finished Goods page, the Product Release list and the run window, show why a lot is on hold, who and when, and whether the release gate passes now. Tell apart a hold placed by the system after a lab result changed (the lab_result_hold event) from a hold set by hand (the fg_lot_edited event and its reason). (4) Chips on the Product Release list: one chip per run, green when every check is met, so ready and stuck runs can be seen without opening each one. (5) Release from hold: a 'Release from hold' button on the same checklist, shown to Quality Managers only, with a required reason. It is enabled only when the release gate passes now; otherwise it is disabled and says which checks are still red. It uses the existing rule for lifting a hold (PUT /api/fg/:id to on_hand), so it needs no new permission and writes the same fg_lot_edited event to the hash chain.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-27. Staging run PR-20260727-001 was released but its finished-goods lot showed status Hold and nobody could see why. Cause: a required lab result was voided after release, so _lab_regate put the lot on hold and logged lab_result_hold; entering a replacement passing result does not lift the hold; only a Quality Manager can lift it. The only evidence was in the audit trail. N. Wrana's point: the problem is not an extra sign-off but that the state of the release gate and the reason for a hold are hard to see. An earlier idea to lift the hold automatically was considered and set aside: lifting a hold stays a deliberate Quality Manager decision. Follows KW-28 and KW-30 (released: review and release view) and the production log's required-fields progress chips (PROGRESS_SECTIONS, stage chips) as the visual pattern. The release gate table already exists in the run window (d.gate); this item makes it a status and checklist, adds the hold cause, and surfaces both on the list and Finished Goods. Must NOT change: the release gate rules, who may release, review or lift a hold, the release snapshot hash (RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_VERSION unchanged), stock, or any stored record. Expected to need no schema change and no new setting: a read-only payload that adds the hold cause, taken from the latest lab_result_hold or fg_lot_edited event of the run or lot. Claude Code to list and confirm in the plan: where each screen gets its hold cause, how a lot with several holds is shown, and the wording. QM-001 impact: visibility only, no control changes; the Quality Manager is told because it touches the release screens.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) The run window and the Product Release list show a status line with the stage, who the run is waiting on, and the next step, for every release state including pending_review, pending_release, released, hold, rejected, amending and legacy. 2) A checklist lists the six checks above; each failing check shows a reason and a link to the right window; a run with every check met shows all green. The gate checks reuse release_gate (no second implementation of the rules). 3) Every Hold badge on Finished Goods, the Product Release list and the run window shows the cause, who, when, and whether the release gate passes now; a hold from a changed lab result and a hold set by hand are labelled differently.
